chapters.summary: In David's old age, Adonijah presumes to make himself king, but with the help of Bathsheba and the prophet Nathan, Solomon is anointed king instead.
keyPoints: As David grows old, Adonijah exalts himself and prepares chariots and horsemen, scheming for the throne.
Bathsheba and Nathan alert David, and David immediately has Solomon anointed king.
When Adonijah's followers hear the news, they scatter in fear, and Solomon's throne is secured.
chapters.application: In all things let us seek God's will rather than act out of impulse. God will surely fulfill his promises, and we should trust his leading, remaining faithful even while we wait.

chapters.summary: On his deathbed David charges Solomon to walk in God's ways and to deal with Joab, Shimei, and Adonijah, and Solomon secures the throne.
keyPoints: David charges Solomon to keep God's law and walk in the LORD's ways so that he may prosper.
Following David's instructions, Solomon deals with Joab and Shimei, and removes Abiathar from the priesthood.
When Adonijah asks to marry Abishag the Shunammite, Solomon puts him to death, securing the throne.
chapters.application: Let us follow Solomon's example of revering God and walking in the LORD's ways, seeking his guidance in all things and handling our affairs with justice and wisdom, so that our lives may be established and blessed.

chapters.summary: King Solomon offers sacrifices at Gibeon, and God appears to him in a dream and promises to give him wisdom; Solomon asks for wisdom to govern the people, and God is pleased and grants him wealth and honor as well.
keyPoints: Solomon secures his throne through marriage to Pharaoh's daughter, but the people are still sacrificing at the high places.
God appears to Solomon in a dream and promises to give him whatever he asks; Solomon asks for wisdom to judge the people.
Because Solomon did not ask for riches or long life, God grants him wisdom, and adds to it wealth and honor besides.
chapters.application: When we face important decisions, let us, like Solomon, humbly ask for wisdom rather than seek only material gain, and God will surely watch over our needs.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how King Solomon organized his administration, appointing twelve officers to supply provisions for the royal household, and describes his wisdom and the nation's prosperity.
keyPoints: Solomon appoints twelve officers who take turns supplying the needs of the royal household each month, ensuring orderly government.
Solomon rules over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt, and they bring tribute and serve him.
Solomon's wisdom surpasses that of all the people of the east and of Egypt; he speaks three thousand proverbs, and his songs number a thousand and five.
chapters.application: Solomon's wisdom came from God. Let us ask for wisdom to manage our own lives, and use our resources well to serve others, so that God's name may be glorified.

chapters.summary: Solomon makes a covenant with Hiram, king of Tyre, to prepare materials for building the temple, and works together with the people in the labor.
keyPoints: Solomon sends messengers to Hiram, asking him to supply cedar and cypress timber for building the temple.
Hiram agrees, providing timber and skilled workers, and the two kings make a covenant, helping one another.
Solomon conscripts forced laborers from Israel, who take turns going up to the mountains to cut timber, while Solomon oversees the progress of the work.
chapters.application: In serving God, let us learn from Solomon's example, humbly seeking help, working in harmony with others, and being willing to labor, so that God's work may be accomplished.

chapters.summary: Solomon builds the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem, a project taking seven years, and this chapter records in detail its dimensions, structure, and decoration.
keyPoints: Solomon begins building the temple in the 480th year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, and it takes seven years to complete.
The interior of the temple is adorned with cedar and pure gold, carved with figures of cherubim and palm trees.
The ark of the covenant is placed in the most holy place, and everything in the temple is built exactly according to the pattern God revealed.
chapters.application: Our own lives are also a temple for God. Let us build them with purity and obedience, so that God may dwell within us and make our lives a dwelling place of glory.

chapters.summary: This chapter details Solomon's building of his palace and the temple, including the House of the Forest of Lebanon, the colonnade, and the making of the bronze pillars, the bronze sea, and the bronze stands for the temple.
keyPoints: Solomon takes thirteen years to build his own palace, including the House of the Forest of Lebanon and the colonnade.
Two bronze pillars are made for the temple, named Jachin and Boaz, and set up before the entrance.
The craftsman Huram makes the bronze sea, the stands, the basins, and other furnishings for the temple with exquisite skill.
chapters.application: Whatever work we do for God, let us do it with all our heart, offering our very best to the Lord, for all glory belongs to him.

chapters.summary: Solomon brings the ark of the covenant into the temple and offers the dedicatory prayer, asking God to attend to the people's prayers and repentance.
keyPoints: Solomon assembles the elders of Israel and brings the ark of the covenant up from the city of David into the most holy place of the temple.
Solomon offers the dedicatory prayer, recounting God's promises and the meaning of the temple.
Solomon intercedes for the people, asking God to hear their prayers offered in the temple and to forgive them.
chapters.application: Today we have no temple, yet we may pray to God at any time. May God hear our cries, forgive our sins, and guide us to walk in the right way.

chapters.summary: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time, promising to establish his throne if he keeps God's statutes and commandments, but warning of punishment if he does not; Solomon also trades with Hiram and builds fortified cities.
keyPoints: God appears to Solomon a second time, reaffirming the terms of the covenant: obedience will secure the throne forever, but rebellion will bring the nation to ruin.
Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities in Galilee; Hiram is not pleased with them, but the two remain on friendly terms.
Solomon conscripts foreign peoples as forced laborers and builds fortified cities such as Millo and Hazor.
chapters.application: Let us hold fast to God's commands with reverence, never growing proud because of temporary success, but continuing in gratitude and obedience, glorifying God in our daily lives.

chapters.summary: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon and marvels at his wisdom and wealth; Solomon amasses vast amounts of gold and silver, though a hint appears of the danger of straying from God's commands.
keyPoints: Hearing of Solomon's wisdom, the Queen of Sheba comes to test him with hard questions, and seeing his palace, his officials, and his burnt offerings, she is left breathless with amazement.
Through gold, ivory, exotic animals, and trading ships, Solomon amasses so much silver and gold that it becomes as common as stone, and his splendor is unrivaled.
Kings of the earth seek an audience to hear Solomon's wisdom, while he amasses horses, chariots, and riches, quietly hinting at a violation of the law for kings given in Deuteronomy.
chapters.application: Let us remember the God who grants wisdom and prosperity, never allowing gifts and achievements to replace our obedience to him, but keeping a humble and grateful heart.

chapters.summary: Because Solomon marries foreign women and follows after other gods, the LORD is angry with him, foretells that the kingdom will be divided, and raises up adversaries against him.
keyPoints: Solomon loves many foreign women, and they turn his heart away to follow idols, leading him away from God.
The LORD is angry with Solomon and declares that he will tear most of the kingdom away from him, leaving him only one tribe.
God raises up Hadad the Edomite, Rezon son of Eliada, and Jeroboam as adversaries against Solomon, foreshadowing the coming division.
chapters.application: Let us be careful in choosing companions and friends, holding fast to our faithfulness to God and guarding against worldly influence, for God searches the heart and will judge according to our deeds.

chapters.summary: After Solomon's death his son Rehoboam refuses the counsel of the elders, causing the northern tribes of Israel to rebel; Jeroboam is made king, and the kingdom is divided into north and south.
keyPoints: Rehoboam goes to Shechem to be made king, and the people ask him to lighten their heavy burden.
Rehoboam rejects the counsel of the elders and follows the advice of the young men instead, answering the people harshly.
The ten tribes of Israel rebel and make Jeroboam king, leaving Judah with only the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.
chapters.application: When facing important decisions, let us humbly seek wisdom, listening to the counsel of our elders and spiritual mentors, lest pride bring about division and loss.

chapters.summary: A man of God, sent by the LORD, pronounces judgment on Jeroboam, but is later killed by a lion for disobeying God's word, showing how important it is to obey God.
keyPoints: The man of God prophesies disaster upon Jeroboam's house, and the altar splits apart with its ashes poured out as a sign.
The man of God refuses the king's gift, because the LORD had commanded him not to eat or drink.
An old prophet deceives the man of God, causing him to disobey God's command, and he is killed by a lion.
chapters.application: Today let us hold fast to God's word, never letting it be shaken by the words of others or by circumstances, lest we stray from the right path and lose God's favor.

chapters.summary: Ahijah prophesies disaster upon Jeroboam's house and the death of his son; Israel is handed over to its enemies, and Judah too is punished for idolatry.
keyPoints: Jeroboam's wife comes in disguise to inquire of him, and the prophet Ahijah pronounces God's severe judgment.
Jeroboam's son Abijah dies and is given an honorable burial, while the rest of the household meets disaster.
Rehoboam king of Judah does evil, and Shishak king of Egypt plunders the treasures of the temple.
chapters.application: Let us turn away from idols and rely wholeheartedly on God. God's judgment is righteous, yet he shows mercy to those who repent. May we hold fast to pure faith in our lives and receive his blessing.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the reigns of Abijam and Asa, kings of Judah, and Nadab and Baasha, kings of Israel, emphasizing the importance of faithfulness to God.
keyPoints: Abijam commits all the sins his father had committed, yet for David's sake God still grants him a lamp.
Asa does what is right in the eyes of the LORD and removes the idols, though the high places are not taken away.
Nadab does evil, and Baasha conspires against him and kills him, fulfilling the word the LORD spoke through Ahijah against Jeroboam's house.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us hold fast to our faithfulness to God, for he will remember our good deeds and grant us grace and protection.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the reigns of Baasha, Elah, Zimri, Omri, and Ahab, kings of Israel, who did evil in the eyes of the LORD, bringing turmoil to the nation and prophetic judgment upon it.
keyPoints: Baasha is judged by God for his sins, and his son Elah is killed after succeeding him.
Zimri usurps the throne for only seven days before he is besieged and burns himself to death.
Omri builds the city of Samaria, and his son Ahab marries Jezebel and worships Baal, provoking God to anger.
chapters.application: Let us be on guard against the temptation of sin, keeping far from idols and wickedness. God sees all things, and we should live with reverence, seeking righteousness and holiness.

chapters.summary: The prophet Elijah is kept safe by God during a drought, and through the widow of Zarephath's jar of meal and jug of oil that never run out, and the raising of her son, God's faithful provision and power are revealed.
keyPoints: Elijah announces the drought and, at God's command, hides by the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him food.
He goes to Zarephath, where a widow welcomes him with what little food she has left, and her jar of meal and jug of oil never run dry.
When the widow's son falls ill and dies, Elijah pleads with the LORD three times, and the boy is restored to life, showing that God is the Lord of life.
chapters.application: In times of lack and hardship, let us follow the example of Elijah and the widow, obeying God in faith and experiencing his daily provision and care, trusting that he is in control of all things.

chapters.summary: Elijah confronts the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, proving that the LORD alone is the true God, and prays for rain to fall, ending the three-year drought.
keyPoints: At God's command Elijah goes to meet Ahab and announces that the three-year drought is about to end.
In the contest on Mount Carmel, the prophets of Baal fail, and Elijah prays and fire falls from heaven.
Elijah prays seven times for rain, and God sends a heavy rain, bringing the drought to an end.
chapters.application: In our life of faith, let us trust wholeheartedly in the one true God, never wavering between two opinions. Elijah's prayer reminds us that persistent prayer will surely be answered, for God watches over our needs.

chapters.summary: Threatened by Jezebel, Elijah flees, and on Mount Horeb he experiences God's presence and receives comfort and a new commission.
keyPoints: Fearing Jezebel's threat, Elijah flees and, in the wilderness, asks to die.
God provides him with food, strengthening him to walk forty days and forty nights to Mount Horeb.
God appears to him in a still small voice, and instructs him to anoint a new king and a new prophet.
chapters.application: In weakness and despair, God understands our limits, guides us through a still small voice, and grants us a new mission and new strength.

chapters.summary: Ben-hadad king of Syria attacks Samaria; God promises Ahab victory through a prophet, but Ahab lets Ben-hadad go free, and the prophet pronounces God's punishment.
keyPoints: Ben-hadad king of Syria gathers a great army to besiege Samaria and makes harsh demands of Ahab.
Through a prophet God promises Ahab victory twice, and the Israelites strike down the Syrians.
Ahab makes a covenant with Ben-hadad and lets him go, and a prophet uses a parable to pronounce God's judgment.
chapters.application: God is faithful, and we should submit fully to his will rather than acting according to our own judgment, lest we lose God's blessing.

chapters.summary: King Ahab covets Naboth's vineyard and is sullen when Naboth refuses to sell it; Queen Jezebel schemes to have Naboth killed by stoning, and Ahab seizes the vineyard, so Elijah pronounces God's judgment on Ahab and Jezebel.
keyPoints: Ahab covets Naboth's vineyard and, when refused, becomes sullen and displeased.
Jezebel forges the king's orders and frames Naboth, bringing about his death.
Elijah pronounces God's judgment on Ahab and Jezebel.
chapters.application: When our desires are denied, let us examine our own hearts rather than harm others out of covetousness. God is just and will surely vindicate the innocent; let us revere God and keep far from all unrighteousness.

chapters.summary: Coveting Ramoth-gilead, King Ahab must choose between the words of the false prophets and the prophecy of Micaiah, and in the end he dies in battle, fulfilling what God had spoken through Elijah and Micaiah.
keyPoints: King Ahab invites Jehoshaphat to join him in attacking Ramoth-gilead, and Jehoshaphat suggests they first inquire of the LORD.
Four hundred false prophets predict victory, but Micaiah faithfully delivers God's true word, prophesying Ahab's death and exposing the false prophets' lies.
Ahab disguises himself for battle but is still struck by an arrow and dies; his blood stains the chariot, and dogs lick it up, fulfilling God's judgment.
chapters.application: When many voices tell us what we want to hear, let us discern carefully, for only God's word is true and reliable. Even when circumstances seem unfavorable, let us submit to God's will, for his promises will surely come to pass.
